correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed from exact stationary-sleeper first-hit representation in Junge–Kaufman–Meisel Proposition 5. Bernoulli refresh preserves independent Bernoulli(p) stationary coordinates even conditional on sink choices; independent exact checks show birth u=(1-q)p(1-y/n), death d=(1-q)(1-p)y/n, drift -(1-q)(y-np)/n, center second moment ->2p(1-p). At t_n=(1-p)n/q_n and time windows n*s, martingale diffusion scaling gives stationary OU, jointly independent sink-count Gaussian G; fluctuation of Z across n steps vanishes on sqrt(n) scale. Doob and binomial-refresh subgaussian maximal bounds localize the first hit from both tails; nondegenerate OU immediate crossing enables hitting-time functional continuity. Distribution at hit equals -(G+c tau)/sigma; shifting the time boundary and reversing stationary OU cancels G, yielding sup_t(X_t-(c/sigma)t). Endpoint path properties follow linear penalty, OU Gaussian increments/ergodicity. Finite checker script examined, but no finite experiment is asserted to prove functional CLT, independence, localization or continuum law.
residual_risks: Localization and independence assumptions are delicate; the convergence is weak only, not uniform moments or convergence rates.
Conditional binomial stationarity depends on exact self-looped complete graph and initial Bernoulli refresh construction.

value.rationale: The finite nonzero critical sink parameter is an explicit open scaling gap between known stationary Gaussian and Gumbel regimes in a natural interacting-particle model. Identifying a nontrivial continuously parameterized OU-supremum crossover has independent mathematical relevance and could inform future asymptotic and finite-size studies.
residual_risks: No claim about joint limits q_n sqrt(n)->0 or infinity, convergence of normalized moments, or explicit distribution function.

final_claim: For complete-graph driven dissipative activated random walk with Bernoulli sleep probability p in (0,1) and sink probability q_n sqrt(n)->c in (0,infinity), the stationary sleeper count (S_n-np)/(sqrt(p(1-p))*sqrt(n)) converges weakly to sup_{t>=0}(X_t-theta t), theta=c/sqrt(p(1-p)), for stationary variance-one OU X; the family has strict stochastic ordering and correct Gaussian/infinite boundary behavior.
limitations: Self-loop complete graph, fixed p, c strictly between 0 and infinity.
No finite-sample rate or expectation/variance convergence.
